Aspire

uh-SPYRE -- the second syllable rhymes with 'fire'. · verb

What It Means

To aspire to have a great ambition or ultimate goal; to strive toward it.

Many young engineers aspire to design the spacecraft that will one day carry astronauts to Mars.

Worked Example

A ten-year-old tapes a photograph of the Supreme Court above her desk and tells everyone who asks that she will argue a case there someday.

Holding a great, guiding ambition -- and orienting your life toward it -- is what it means to aspire. Unlike a passing wish, an aspiration is a lofty goal that shapes what you work toward every day.

How Aspire Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

aim

aim: to direct one's efforts toward a goal

strive

strive: to make great efforts to achieve something

yearn

yearn: to long deeply for something

Antonyms

settle

settle: to accept something less than one hoped for

stagnate

stagnate: to stop developing or making progress

How Strong Is It? — aim → aspire → strive

aim vs. aspire

aim vs. aspire: Aim is flatter and more practical than aspire -- you can aim to finish your homework by six, while to aspire is reserved for lofty, long-range ambitions that shape a whole path.

strive vs. aspire

strive vs. aspire: Strive is more effortful than aspire: to aspire emphasizes holding the great goal in your sights, while to strive emphasizes the active struggling and laboring you do to reach it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — a-

prefix — a-: to, toward (variant of Latin ad-)

root — spire

root — spire: to breathe (from Latin spirare)

Put it together

Put it together: Aspire comes from Latin ad- ('toward') -- worn down to a- -- plus spirare ('to breathe'), spelled spire here: literally 'to breathe toward' something. The image is of longing so strong you can feel it in your breath, reaching toward a goal above you.

Use the root in a new word: inspire

Use the root in a new word: inspire: The astronaut's speech managed to inspire half the auditorium to join the school's rocketry club.

Root Check

Word Choice

Aspire is nearly always followed by 'to' -- either 'aspire to' plus a verb ('aspire to become a surgeon') or plus a noun ('aspire to greatness'). It is the natural verb for ambition: the goal is high, and the aspirer is determined to climb toward it.
